subject: POC success gates + traffic intake (RPS / bursts / token profiling)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@greenfieldhealth.com>, Maya Powell <maya.powell@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: POC success gates + traffic intake (RPS / bursts / token profiling)

Hi Ethan / Maya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed concrete next steps so we can stand up the trial environment next week. I’ve kept this to the items we discussed plus a few clarifying questions.

Summary (high level)
- Goal: 30-day evaluation to validate model quality and production economics for Greenfield Health’s conversational triage feature.
- Acceptance gates: quality (NPS-style synthetic queries), latency (p95 < 450ms end-to-end for 256-token requests), and cost per 1k tokens target.

Traffic profile (we need your confirmation / samples)
- Baseline RPS: 8 requests/sec average daytime workload (Mon-Fri 9am–6pm PT).
- Concurrency: typical 24 concurrent sessions, peak concurrency 80 during bursts.
- Burst behavior: 6–8 short bursts/day, each lasting ~90–240 seconds with spike to 220–250 RPS for 60–120s.
- Token lengths: prompt median ~110 tokens, median completion ~60 tokens; 95th percentile combined ~520 tokens. Please send ~200 sample requests if possible.

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Functional: >= 92% intent-match on the curated eval set (we’ll run the same prompt set).
2) Performance: p95 latency <450ms for 256-token requests, no errors >0.5% over 24h windows.
3) Stability: no out-of-memory or tail-latency spikes during three representative burst windows.

Operational owners
- Redwood: Ben (trial infra, capacity routing), Jasmine (eval-run coordination).
- Greenfield: Ethan (product), Maya (platform / data).

Next steps
1) Ethan/Maya: share token_sample CSV and a short list of 20 critical user queries (by 2026-09-24). Attachments: greenfield_token_samples.csv (recommended format included).
2) Redwood: provision trial cluster (dedicated pool) and baseline model variant; we’ll share a timing calendar by EOD 2026-09-23.
3) Joint: kickoff smoke run (20k tokens) and an acceptance readout at day 7.

Questions for Greenfield
- Do you have any hard SLA thresholds for 99th percentile latency we should know about?
- Will we be routing any PII-sensitive fields through the model that would change our recommendation for private deployment?

Attachments: sample CSV template and trial matrix attached.

Thanks — I’ll be on standby to take the token samples and book the cluster.

—
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0133
From: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Maya Powell <maya.powell@greenfieldhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success gates + traffic intake (RPS / bursts / token profiling)

Thanks Jasmine — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Token samples: attaching a first pass (greenfield_token_samples.csv). The prompt column includes PHI placeholders; we can strip anything that would count as real PHI for the initial smoke test.
- Bursts: the 220–250 RPS spikes occur when our morning appointment reminders batch executes; they’re short (usually 45–90s). We can schedule the first smoke run to align with a non-peak window to start.
- 99th percentile: our current internal threshold is 700ms, but customers notice anything >500ms. We’d like p95 <400ms if feasible, but p95 <450ms is acceptable for the POC.

Also looping in Maya for platform constraints — Maya, will Greenfield require a VPC-only connection for the trial? If yes, we’ll need the network ACL and IP allowlist.

—
Ethan Ross
Head of Product, Greenfield Health
ethan.ross@greenfieldhealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0234
From: Maya Powell <maya.powell@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>, Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success gates + traffic intake (RPS / bursts / token profiling)

Thanks — quick note on infra: Greenfield prefers a VPC-peering setup for POCs involving real customer queues. We can do a limited allowlist and a temporary subnet. I’ll share the network ACL + allowlist by EOD 2026-09-24.

Also, Ben — can you confirm whether Redwood needs any special headers for tracing (trace-id or request-id) so our telemetry team can correlate events during the smoke run?

Maya
Platform Engineering, Greenfield Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maya Powell <maya.powell@greenfieldhealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@greenfieldhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC success gates + traffic intake (RPS / bursts / token profiling)

Maya — yes, please send the ACL + allowlist when ready. For tracing we prefer the following headers: X-Request-Id and X-Trace-Id; adding X-Client-Session helps tie multiple requests to a session for the eval. We’ll instrument our side to accept them and surface traces in the trial dashboard.

Operational timeline (updated)
- 2026-09-24: Greenfield sends token samples + ACL (EOD).
- 2026-09-25: Redwood provisions the dedicated trial cluster and posts access details.
- 2026-09-28: Baseline smoke run (non-peak) — 20k tokens.
- 2026-10-05: Day-7 acceptance readout and metric handoff.

I’ll attach the trial matrix workbook (po_trial_matrix.xlsx) to the shared Drive and update the HubSpot milestone once the cluster is live.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
